requirement: In Markdown, escaped roles and role-looking text in inline code, fenced code, or raw HTML MUST remain literal and MUST NOT count as references. Raw HTML means an HTML block, an HTML comment, or an inline HTML tag including its attributes; text between inline tags is ordinary Markdown. A `{req}` directive inside a fenced code example and a legacy inline `{req}` role MUST NOT define a requirement.
rationale: I judge the tests adequate. They cover each obligation in `requirements.references.markdown_literals`, and their assertions check outcomes. I did not request implementation source. The test text was enough to map every clause. - **Escaped roles stay literal.** - `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[every_markdown_extension_keeps_escaped_and_code_roles_literal]` includes `\{role}` and asserts that no reference comes from any Markdown file. - `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[markdown_examples_and_escaped_references_stay_literal]` runs the preprocessor and asserts that the escaped role leaves the content intact. - The same lib.rs test also covers backslash parity. `\\{marker}` is not escaped, `\\\{marker}` is, and `roles.len()==1` at `start==2` pins this. - **Inline code stays literal.** - The evidence.rs test, the lib.rs preprocessor test and `src/terms.rs#mod[tests]/fn[term_dependencies_of_every_markdown_extension_skip_literal_roles]` each include a role in backticks. - `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[code_examples_and_legacy_roles_remain_literal]` uses a double-backtick span. - **Fenced code stays literal.** - Roles inside ```` ```text ```` fences are tested in evidence.rs, in the lib.rs preprocessor test and in terms.rs. - The evidence.rs test also puts a `:::{cite}` directive fence inside a code fence. - `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[references_in_requirement_bodies_are_scanned_as_markdown]` covers a fence inside a requirement body. - **Raw HTML stays literal, and text between inline tags is ordinary Markdown.** - `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[roles_in_raw_html_stay_literal]` covers an HTML block, a block comment, an inline comment and an attribute value. It asserts that only the role between `` and `` counts as a reference. It also asserts that 5 roles count in non-Markdown mode. - `src/fenced.rs#mod[tests]/fn[markdown_fences_in_raw_html_stay_literal]` covers directive fences inside a block, a comment and a multi-line tag attribute. It asserts that only the outside fence counts, and that all fences count in plain-text mode. - The evidence.rs test, terms.rs and `tests/definitions.rs#fn[literal_term_roles_in_subject_and_requirements_inputs_need_no_definition]` cover the attribute case for other role kinds. - **A `{req}` directive in a fenced code example does not define a requirement.** `code_examples_and_legacy_roles_remain_literal` has an indented `:::{req} block` inside a fence. It asserts that the text stays literal while the real `visible` directive is rendered as a requirement. - **A legacy inline `{req}` role does not define a requirement.** `code_examples_and_legacy_roles_remain_literal` and `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[colon_directives_render_markdown_bodies_and_legacy_roles_stay_literal]` assert that `{req}`legacy`` and `{req}`inline`` stay literal and produce no `habeas-req-requirements.inline` anchor. - **Markdown versus non-Markdown files.** The evidence.rs and terms.rs tests cover `.md`, `.markdown`, `.MD` and `.Markdown`. Each uses `.txt` as a negative control, which shows the literal rules apply only to Markdown. I found no named obligation or boundary without a test that asserts its outcome.
